quick: 1 g IV/IM every 8-12 hours (range 1-2 g q8-12h)
Use only if clearly needed; generally low risk
Renal function, signs of allergy, superinfection
summary: Ceftazidime is a parenteral third-generation cephalosporin with potent activity against Gram-negative bacteria, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and stability against many beta-lactamases. It is used for serious respiratory, urinary, intra-abdominal, skin, bone, gynecologic and CNS infections, septicemia and febrile neutropenia. The usual adult dose is 1 g IV/IM every 8-12 hours, adjusted for renal function.
indications: Lower respiratory tract infections, including pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas and other susceptible Gram-negatives
Gynecologic, intra-abdominal infections and bacterial meningitis caused by susceptible organisms

dosage.d: 1 g IV or IM every 8 to 12 hours
After 1 g loading: 1 g q12h (CrCl 31-50), q24h (16-30), 500 mg q24h (6-15), 500 mg q48h (<5)

admin: Reconstitute and administer by direct IV injection over 3-5 minutes, by intermittent IV infusion over 15-30 minutes, or by deep IM injection into a large muscle
Carbon dioxide is released on reconstitution; vent the vial as directed
For IM use, may reconstitute with lidocaine to reduce injection pain per label
Do not mix in the same syringe or infusion line with aminoglycosides; flush lines between drugs
Use prepared solutions promptly; observe storage and color-change guidance
moa: Ceftazidime is a bactericidal beta-lactam that binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell-wall (peptidoglycan) synthesis, leading to cell lysis. Its aminothiazolyl and carboxypropyl-oxyimino side chains confer enhanced stability against many Gram-negative beta-lactamases and broad activity including Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to ceftazidime or other cephalosporins
relative: History of immediate-type penicillin allergy (cross-reactivity risk)
monitor: Patients with seizure risk in renal failure (neurotoxicity)

preg: Cephalosporins, including ceftazidime, are generally considered low risk; there are no adequate well-controlled studies. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Ceftazidime is excreted in human milk in low concentrations and is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding; observe the infant for diarrhea, thrush or rash.
renal: Dosage must be reduced in renal impairment because ceftazidime is excreted almost entirely by the kidneys. After a 1 g loading dose, adjust by creatinine clearance (e.g. 1 g q12h for CrCl 31-50, q24h for 16-30, 500 mg q24h for 6-15, 500 mg q48h for <5 mL/min). Give a supplemental dose after each hemodialysis session.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required in hepatic impairment; ceftazidime is eliminated renally as unchanged drug.

major: No major contraindicated drug interactions established
moderate: Aminoglycosides and potent diuretics (furosemide) - additive nephrotoxicity; monitor renal function
Chloramphenicol - possible antagonism of bactericidal effect in vitro
Probenecid - limited effect on ceftazidime (largely glomerular filtration)
minor: Live typhoid/BCG vaccines - antibacterials may reduce efficacy
Oral anticoagulants - cephalosporins may rarely prolong prothrombin time
interactions.alcohol: No disulfiram-like reaction (ceftazidime lacks the N-methylthiotetrazole side chain).
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive urine glucose test with copper-reduction methods and a positive direct Coombs test.

serious: Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures) in renal failure

monitoring: Renal function at baseline and during therapy, especially with concomitant nephrotoxins
Signs of hypersensitivity, particularly in penicillin-allergic patients
Complete blood count and liver enzymes on prolonged therapy
Neurologic status in renal impairment; evaluate persistent diarrhea for C. difficile
counsel: Report rash, hives, swelling or difficulty breathing immediately
Tell staff about any penicillin or cephalosporin allergy
Report severe or persistent diarrhea during or after treatment
Complete the full course of therapy
pk: Rapid bactericidal effect after IV dosing
End of IV infusion; ~1 hour after IM
Store dry powder per label; refrigerate reconstituted solution and use within labeled time
pearls: Reliable antipseudomonal coverage among cephalosporins; a workhorse for hospital Gram-negative infections
Dose strictly by renal function - accumulation can cause encephalopathy, myoclonus and seizures
No disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol (unlike cefoperazone/cefotetan)
Do not co-infuse with aminoglycosides; give in separate lines
missed: For scheduled inpatient dosing, give the missed dose as soon as possible and adjust the schedule so the interval to the next dose is appropriate; do not give two doses together. Maintain the prescribed dosing interval, especially in renal impairment.
overdose: Overdose, particularly in renal impairment, can cause neurologic sequelae including encephalopathy, asterixis, myoclonus and seizures. Manage supportively; reduce or hold dosing and correct renal function. Ceftazidime is removed by hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis, which can be used to lower serum levels.
